chapter_title: Day 5: The End of Empire and the Birth of Modern Turkey
learning_objective: The learner will classify fourteen places on a map of the former Ottoman Empire by the era in which they left Ottoman rule, classifying at least 10 of 14 correctly on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: map **sim-id:** ottoman-retreat-map
**Library:** Leaflet
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify fourteen places on a map of the former Ottoman Empire by the era in which they left Ottoman rule, classifying at least 10 of 14 correctly on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Ottoman decline, the treaties of Karlowitz (1699) and Küçük Kaynarca (1774), nationalism, the Congress of Berlin (1878), the Balkan Wars, World War I (all introduced in the section "Ottoman Decline" above; World War I is detailed in Part Two). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of the fourteen places, the learner commits one of four eras before the answer is revealed. A choice is correct when it matches the Correct era column in Content. Mastery is 10 of 14 correct on the first attempt. Panning the map and opening place labels is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The Greek and Balkan lands were the last to go, because they were closest to Istanbul. (2) The Arab provinces broke away early. (3) The empire lost its lands in one collapse in 1918. (4) Every lost place became an independent nation at once, when many passed first to another empire (Russia, France, Britain, Italy). **Instructional Rationale:** Committing to an era for each place before the reveal makes the learner test a mental model of the retreat against the map. Replaying the four eras in order afterward turns fourteen separate answers into one picture: the empire withdrew from the edges of Europe first and from the Arab lands last. **Content:** The four eras, as the learner sees them: - Era 1: 1683–1829 (from the siege of Vienna to the eve of Greek independence) - Era 2: 1830–1878 (from Greek independence to the Congress of Berlin) - Era 3: 1879–1913 (to the end of the Balkan Wars) - Era 4: 1914–1923 (World War I and after) Two reference places are shown but not scored: Istanbul (41.01, 28.98), "Ottoman capital until 1922; Turkish ever since," and Ankara (39.93, 32.86), "capital of the Republic of Turkey from 1923." | # | Place (lat, lon) | What happened | Correct era | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Buda, today part of Budapest (47.50, 19.04) | Taken by Habsburg forces in 1686; Hungary ceded at Karlowitz in 1699 | Era 1 | Hungary was the first large, permanent loss, a generation after the failed siege of Vienna. | | 2 | Bakhchysarai, capital of the Crimean Khanate (44.75, 33.88) | Made independent of the sultan in 1774; annexed by Russia in 1783 | Era 1 | Crimea went to Russia long before any Balkan nation became independent. | | 3 | Athens (37.97, 23.73) | Greece recognized as independent in 1830; Ottoman garrison left the Acropolis in 1833 | Era 2 | Greece was the first Christian people of the empire to win full independence. | | 4 | Algiers (36.75, 3.06) | Conquered by France in 1830 | Era 2 | Algiers passed to another empire, France, not to independence. | | 5 | Belgrade (44.82, 20.46) | Serbia self-governing from 1830; last Ottoman garrison left in 1867; independence recognized in 1878 | Era 2 | Serbia left in stages over half a century, completed at the Congress of Berlin. | | 6 | Nicosia, Cyprus (35.17, 33.36) | Placed under British administration in 1878 | Era 2 | Britain took over Cyprus at the Congress of Berlin while it stayed nominally Ottoman. | | 7 | Cairo (30.04, 31.24) | Occupied by Britain in 1882 | Era 3 | Egypt had long run its own affairs; British troops made the break final in 1882. | | 8 | Heraklion, Crete (35.34, 25.13) | Autonomous Cretan State from 1898; united with Greece in 1913 | Era 3 | Crete left the empire as an autonomous state first and joined Greece fifteen years later. | | 9 | Rhodes (36.44, 28.22) | Taken by Italy in 1912 | Era 3 | Rhodes went to Italy, not Greece, in the Italo-Turkish War, and was handed to Greece only in 1947, with formal union in 1948. | | 10 | Thessaloniki (40.64, 22.94) | Taken by Greece in 1912, in the First Balkan War | Era 3 | Atatürk's birthplace became Greek when he was 31. | | 11 | Mecca (21.42, 39.83) | Arab Revolt began in 1916; the Hejaz became independent | Era 4 | The Arab provinces stayed Ottoman until World War I. | | 12 | Baghdad (33.31, 44.36) | Taken by Britain in 1917 | Era 4 | Mesopotamia, ruled from Istanbul since 1534, fell only in the war. | | 13 | Jerusalem (31.78, 35.22) | Taken by Britain in 1917 | Era 4 | Jerusalem had been Ottoman since 1517 and fell four centuries later, in December 1917. | | 14 | Damascus (33.51, 36.29) | Taken by British and Arab forces in 1918 | Era 4 | Syria was among the very last provinces lost, in the final weeks of the war. | **Provenance:** Event years from this chapter's section "Ottoman Decline" and its table where stated (1699, 1774–1783, 1830, 1878, 1912, 1913); the others from the Wikipedia articles "Battle of Buda (1686)", "Russian annexation of Crimea", "French conquest of Algeria", "Principality of Serbia", "Cyprus Convention", "Anglo-Egyptian War", "Cretan State", "Italo-Turkish War", "Arab Revolt", "Fall of Baghdad (1917)", "Battle of Jerusalem (1917)", and "Capture of Damascus (1918)". Coordinates are standard city-center values rounded to two decimals; copy them into the sim's data file as given. **Rules:** Each place is answered once for scoring, in the order listed. A first-attempt answer is correct if and only if it equals the Correct era. Score is 0 to 14; mastery is score >= 10. Two places have events in more than one year: Serbia is scored Era 2, because 1830, 1867, and 1878 all fall in Era 2; Crete is scored by its first departure from direct Ottoman rule, 1898 (Era 3), and its feedback says so. After all fourteen are answered, the learner can replay the eras: each step shows the places lost by the end of that era, cumulatively. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the map with all fourteen places marked but unlabeled by era, and the two reference places. 2. For each place in order, the learner reads the "What happened" text and chooses an era. 3. The marker takes its correct era and the feedback appears. 4. After place 14, the learner steps through Era 1 to Era 4; at each step, the places lost by then are marked as lost. 5. The learner should notice that the Balkan and Black Sea lands were lost before 1914 and the Arab lands only during the war. **Feedback:** After each first attempt: correct shows "Correct:" and the Why text; incorrect shows "This place left in [correct era]:" and the Why text. A running count "Correct: n of 14" is shown. At the end: if score >= 10, "You can see the shape of the retreat: Europe's edges first, the Arab lands last."; otherwise, "Look again at the Arab cities and at Rhodes: which ones stayed Ottoman until the very end?" A Try Again option resets all fourteen. **Starting State:** The map of the eastern Mediterranean, the Balkans, and the Middle East, with fourteen unmarked places, and the question "In which era did each place leave the Ottoman Empire?" **Chapter Anchors:** Siege of Vienna 1683; Karlowitz 1699; Crimea independent 1774 and annexed 1783; Greece and Algiers 1830; Congress of Berlin 1878; Rhodes and Thessaloniki 1912; Crete to Greece 1913; fourteen places; four eras; mastery 10 of 14.
